response.answer: Current trends emphasize integrated ecosystem service valuation, advanced land use change assessment, and robust uncertainty analysis for policy scenario modeling. These approaches enhance decision-making in business, economics, and management.

results.title: Ecosystem Services and Biodiversity Conservation amid a Global Pandemic: Insights from the Greater Limpopo Transfrontier Conservation Area | IntechOpen
results.content: Open Access is an initiative that aims to make scientific research freely available to all. As PhD students, we found it difficult to access the research we needed, so we decided to create a new Open Access publisher that levels the playing field for scientists across the world. We are a community of more than 103,000 authors and editors from 3,291 institutions spanning 160 countries, including Nobel Prize winners and some of the world’s most-cited researchers. # Ecosystem Services and Biodiversity Conservation amid a Global Pandemic: Insights from the Greater Limpopo Transfrontier Conservation Area. DOI: 10.5772/intechopen.1011146. This chapter discusses the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on community access to and perceptions of ecosystem services within transfrontier conservation areas (TFCAs), revealing how a global crisis can reshape human-nature relationships and dependencies on natural resources. “The key concepts of the origins of ecosystem services (ESs) come from different definitions associated with their functions in specific contexts.” For example, from an economic viewpoint, they are defined as “flows of value to human societies as a result of the state and quantity of the natural capital” [1].
